1. Leave granted.

sentences.text:
To the extent relevant, the same reads as follows:-
13. Report of Public analyst.2 [(1) The public analyst shall deliver, in such form as may be prescribed, a report to the Local (Health) Authority of the result of the analysis of any article of food submitted to him for analysis.
(2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub- section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the person from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.

Drawing our attention to the document titled Form VI (under Rule 12 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,1955) being the seizure of 100 grams of Table Margarine, Mr. Luthra submits that the seized sample of margarine packed in April 2004 had a shelf life of six months, i.e., till October, 2004.

However, no copy of the report of analysis under Section 13(1) of the PFA Act was shared with the appellants, with the result that they were deprived of their statutory right to apply for analysis of the sample by the Central Food Laboratory.
7. From the facts recorded by the High Court in paragraph 19, extracted supra, it is clear that the provision contained in Section 13(2) of the PFA Act was observed in the breach.

The appellants were not given the 1 PFA Act opportunity to seek a further examination and analysis of the sample of margarine which was seized, before its shelf life ended in October, 2004, by the Central Food Laboratory.
Thus, an error has crept in the proceedings which is not curable.
8. Even otherwise, we are of the view that the incident having taken place in 2004, it would amount to abuse of the process if the prosecution were allowed to continue with the prosecution.
9. Exercising our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, we quash RCC No.339 of 2009 and subsequent proceedings.
10. The appeals stand allowed.
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
